decisions.reason: CH02 defines corruption and its types (bribery, embezzlement, graft); CH25 operationalizes this framework by mandating anticorruption programs and establishing an agency to combat these specific forms.

CH54 introduces NLP as a specific screening technique; CH56 expands on advanced screening methods (including fuzzy logic and AI) and their calibration, directly developing the technological screening framework.

CH56 discusses ongoing testing and calibration of monitoring systems; CH51 discusses piloting AI solutions and setting expectations. They share a broad operational context but do not have a direct framework dependency.

CH42 provides the concrete CDD framework (assessing structure, ownership, BO/UBO); CH16 applies and specializes this framework for high-risk businesses by mandating enhanced due diligence and monitoring based on those exact CDD elements.

CH31 defines the FIU mandate and analysis types; CH34 details senior management AFC responsibilities. These are distinct topics within the broader AFC ecosystem without a direct structural dependency.

CH19 establishes the FATF framework for AML/CFT programs and CDD; CH24 operationalizes this framework specifically for cryptoassets via the FTR regulation, applying the same foundational principles to a new sector.
CH06 classifies PEP types; CH41 details governance committee composition. The PEP classification is not a structural framework that the governance committee composition directly expands or applies.

CH40 provides the key rules for AML governance (dynamic, risk-based policies, regular reviews); CH30 applies these rules by prescribing specific actions to review red flags and implement changes based on reports and guidance.

CH36 defines the Risk Appetite Statement (RAS) and its criteria; CH37 expands on the Enterprise-wide Risk Assessment (EWRA), which is the direct operational process used to evaluate risks against and determine the RAS.

CH54 discusses national identity databases and honeypot risks for eKYC; CH57 is a case study on identifying data for a TM system. They share data management themes but no direct structural illustration or grounding relationship.
